title: How much does an answering service cost?
summary: Answering services range from $25 to $2,000+ a month or $1.65 to $5.00 per minute. Here is why price ranges vary so widely, and how to work out your actual bill.
body_markdown:
Today, affordable AI and human-powered[answering services](https://www.quo.com/answering-service) make it possible to answer every call without blowing your budget.


Answering services are priced a few different ways, which is why quoted costs vary so much. Per-minute bundled plans for AI answering start around $165 a month for 100 minutes and reach $1,380 for 1,000 minutes (Abby Connect). Per-call bundled plans for AI answering start at $25 a month for 40 AI-answered calls and reach $199 for 600 calls ([Quo’s Sona](https://support.quo.com/core-concepts/ai-automations/sona/sona-pricing) ).


Per-minute bundled plans for live virtual receptionists start around $250 a month for 50 minutes and reach $1,725 for 500 minutes ([Ruby](https://www.quo.com/blog/ruby-receptionist-alternatives/) ). Per-call bundled plans for live answering start around $300 a month for 30 calls and reach $2,100 for 300 calls ([Smith ai](https://www.quo.com/blog/smith-ai-alternatives/) ).


Those are bundled plans, the most common setup. But two other models can be cheaper for the right volume: pay-as-you-go which bills only for what you use (roughly $0.15-$0.24 per AI minute), and flat-rate unlimited AI plans that start around $20 a month.


Your actual bill depends on a few things: how many calls or minutes you need, whether you choose AI or human answering, your pricing model, and the cost of overage calls or minutes.


Let’s break down answering service costs, what factors impact it, and how to save money on your pick.


##


Why answering service costs vary so widely


Search this question and you’ll get answers ranging from $25 a month to $2,000+. Both numbers are real. But they’re not describing very different things.


The spread comes down to how answering services are packaged. Most fall into one of four models:


1. Bundled minutes for a monthly price.
2. Bundled calls for a monthly price.
3. Pay-as-you-go per call or per minute, with a monthly base rate.
4. A flat price for unlimited calls or minutes (mostly for AI services; rare for live receptionists)


On top of the pricing model, you’ll also choose how calls are handled:


- AI-handled calls
- Calls handled by a[live virtual receptionist](https://www.quo.com/blog/what-is-a-virtual-receptionist/)


At the same call volume, these pricing models create totally different bills. As you’d expect, calls handled by an AI receptionist sit at the lower end of the range, while live answering typically runs several times more.


##


Answering service pricing models, with real rates


Most[virtual receptionist costs](https://www.quo.com/blog/virtual-receptionist-cost/) follow one of four pricing models:


Model Typical rate for AI answering Typical rate for human answering Best for


Monthly price with bundled minutes $165–$1,300+ per month $250–$1,725+ per month Steady volume with short, predictable calls


Monthly price with bundled calls $25–$200+ per month $300–$1,200+ per month Calls that run long or vary a lot in length


Pay-as-you-go $0 per month + $0.15–$0.24 per minute $25–$65+ per month + $2–$5 per minute Low, variable, or seasonal volume


Flat price for unlimited calls or minutes $20–$199 per month N/A High or unpredictable volume


Let’s break these down in detail:


### 1. Per-minute pricing


Some answering services offer a monthly package with a set number of minutes. Then, any minutes over your limit are charged at per-minute rates — so you might pay $100 per month for a package of 100 minutes, plus $3 extra per additional minute.


**Example per-minute billing:** Abby Connect is a live answering service that charges $165 per month for 100 AI-answered minutes. They don’t publicize their overage rates, but[third-party sources](https://smith.ai/virtual-receptionist-service-comparison/smith-ai-vs-abby-connect) estimate it at between $2.76-$3.29 per minute, depending on your plan. This unlocks features like their Spanish answering service, appointment scheduling, and the option for 24/7 support.


### 2. Per-call pricing


With per-call pricing, you pay a monthly rate for a certain number of calls.Then, any calls over your limit are charged per-call rates — so you might pay $100 per month for a package of 100 calls, plus $3 extra per call.


The per-call pricing model makes it easier to budget, since you only need to estimate your average number of calls each month.


**Example per-call pricing:** Quo’s Sona AI agent plans offer a tiered system so that you pay only for what you need. You get your first 10 calls free, then plans start at $25 per month for 40 calls. Easily scale to a different tier as your business grows without needing to hire additional reps. That way, you can[reduce your customer service costs](https://www.quo.com/blog/reduce-customer-service-costs/) .


Tier 1 Tier 2 Tier 3 Tier 4 Tier 5

Included credits 1,000 credits/10 calls 4,000 credits/40 calls 10,000 credits/100 calls 25,000 credits/250 calls 60,000 credits/600 calls


Overage rate per call $1.00 $0.75 $0.65 $0.55 $0.45


You’ll also get access to features like message-taking, call transcripts and summaries, and integrations with HubSpot, Salesforce, Zapier, Make, and Jobber.


### 3. Pay-as-you-go


With pay-as-you-go, there’s no bundle to buy upfront. Instead of pre-purchasing a block of minutes or calls, you pay only for what you actually use. There may also be a monthly base fee, especially for live receptionist services. The biggest advantage is that you never pay for minutes sitting unused in a package.


The tradeoff is predictability. Because your bill tracks your call volume directly, a busy month costs more than a quiet one. That makes pay-as-you-go a good fit for low or variable call volume or for businesses using an answering service as an emergency backup.


**Example pay-as-you-go pricing:** Synthflow is a no-code AI voice platform that runs on a pure usage model. There’s no monthly platform fee, and you’re billed only for successful calls. Its effective rate typically lands between $0.15 and $0.24 per minute once you factor in the voice engine, language model, and telephony. For live answering, Posh charges a $65 per month base fee plus $2.30 per minute.


### 4. Flat price for unlimited calls or minutes


With flat-rate pricing, you pay one fixed monthly price for unlimited calls or minutes. No bundle to use, no overage charges, no per-minute meter. Your busiest month costs the same as your slowest, which makes budgeting easy.


This model is almost entirely an AI one. Because a live receptionist can only field so many calls, truly unlimited human answering is rare. Some unlimited plans may not actually be unlimited. For example, SkipCalls claims to be unlimited but limits you to 200 calls a month.


**Example flat-rate pricing:** NextPhone is an AI answering service that charges $199 per month for unlimited inbound calls with 24/7 coverage. That flat rate includes features like multilingual answering, an agent trained on your business’s own services and pricing, and no separate per-call or overage fees.

##


Factors that can influence answering service pricing


Other factors besides call volume may increase pricing:


- **Call transfers:** Some platforms won’t let you transfer or forward calls at all without upgrading your plan for more transfer destinations.
- **Appointment scheduling:** Tools like Rosie require you to upgrade before sending appointment links to callers.
- **Bilingual support:** For example, tools like Smith.ai charge an extra $1 per call for agents who are fluent in both English and Spanish. Most AI services include bilingual agents at no extra cost.
- **CRM integrations:** There might be extra fees to connect with popular platforms like HubSpot, Salesforce, and Zendesk.
- **Voicemail to email:** Some platforms automatically send notifications to your inbox, while others tack on extra fees to do the same.
- **Local or toll-free numbers:** You *might* be able to port an existing number, but even then, look out for sneaky porting fees.
- **HIPAA compliance.** Some services like Abby Connect offer HIPAA compliance options, but you’ll have to call for pricing.
- **24/7 or after-hours coverage:** AI services typically include 24/7 coverage at no extra cost. But human answering services often charge a premium for nights, weekends, and holidays.


Speaking of hidden costs…


##


Hidden fees to watch for with answering service costs


Not all answering services charge only what you see on the pricing page.


Keep your eyes peeled for those not-so-transparent additional costs, including:


- **Setup fees:** Some services charge an onboarding or setup fee for first-time customers. For example, Answer Connect charges a $49.99 setup fee before starting any receptionist subscription.
- **Overage charges:** Per-minute pricing will add up fast when your call volume exceeds your plan’s limits. If you get lots of calls during the holidays, for example, you might get an unexpected bill at the end of the month.
- **Long contracts:** Month-to-month plans often cost more than annual ones. But annual pricing usually means a contract — and you could get stuck with a service you no longer want.
- **Early termination fees:** If you *do* decide to end a contract early, or if you don’t cancel within the fine-print window, you might get charged high fees.
- **Billing increments:** Some vendors round each minute up. For example, a 60-second increment turns a 12-second call into a billed minute.
- **Spam and wrong numbers:** Services like Quo don’t charge you for calls under 15 seconds, but not every provider operates that way.
- **Agent work time:** Live receptionist services might charge billable minutes for time an agent spends on your account while not on a call, but doing follow-up work.
- **The 13th invoice:** Some services may charge in four-week billing cycles, meaning 13 invoices a year, not 12.

##


The ROI on answering services


Are the answering service costs making you doubt whether it’s the right choice after all? It might be an investment, but think of the cost of letting those calls go unanswered instead. Use this formula to gauge your ROI:


Estimated monthly missed revenue = Monthly missed calls × Close rate × Average customer value


For example, say you miss 20 calls a month, close 30% of the leads who do reach you, and your average job is worth $500. Your missed revenue is:


20 × 0.3 × $500 = $3,000 in missed revenue every month


That’s more than what most answering services actually cost to run. Want to run more scenarios? Use our free[missed call cost calculator](https://www.quo.com/tools/missed-call-cost-calculator) to see how much money a service like Sona saves you every month.


##


Verdict: Is an answering service worth it?


For most businesses fielding more than a handful of calls a month, yes. The revenue from one missed call that closes usually clears the monthly fee with room to spare. The harder question isn’t *whether* to get one, it’s *which billing model* to get, because the cheapest service is rarely the one with the lowest advertised rate. It’s the one whose model matches your call pattern.


High volumes of short calls run up the bill fast on per-call pricing. Long calls do the same on per-minute. Spiky, unpredictable months eat through a bundle and dump you into overage. And flat-rate makes you pay for calls or minutes you never touch if your volume is low. Work out your typical monthly call volume and average call length first. Then, compare numbers, because the same $150 buys different things across models.

##


FAQs


****How much does outsourced call answering cost?****


Answering service providers charge between $20 and $2,000+ per month, depending on the type and pricing structure. There might be additional costs for minutes that exceed your plan amount or features such as sending booking links via text or scheduling appointments.


**What’s a billing increment, and why does it change your answering service cost?**


A[billing increment](https://www.unitedworldtelecom.com/blog/how-voip-calls-are-charged-understanding-billing-increments/) is the smallest unit a vendor will bill, and most round every call up to it. At a 60-second increment, a 12-second wrong number costs you a full minute, and so does a 58-second one. Many vendors don’t publish their increment up front, so ask before you sign, and assume 60 seconds if they won’t answer. On a per-minute plan this is one of the largest gaps between your quoted rate and your actual invoice.


**What’s the typical cost of a HIPAA-compliant medical answering service?**


Most small practices pay around[$50 to $250 a month](https://www.alliancevirtualoffices.com/virtual-office-blog/hipaa-medical-answering-service/) for roughly 150 calls, though high-volume or 24/7 operations can run well past $1,000. Watch for HIPAA handling as a line item. Many providers charge an extra fee on top of the base rate rather than including it.


****How do you estimate the cost of an answering service for your business?****


First, consider your up-front costs. Then, factor in call volume and your average business call duration.


Finally, decide on per-minute or per-call rates.


You might also need to consider additional costs for specific features such as appointment scheduling or bilingual answering.


****What’s the difference between an answering machine and an answering service?****


An answering machine lets callers leave voicemail messages if you’re out for the day or away from your phone. In contrast, an answering service, also known as an AI receptionist, picks up the phone call and gives callers next steps when you’re busy with other tasks.
